newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian military supports anti-torture law.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian military supports anti-torture law.

text.p: Indonesia's armed forces (ABRI) will support an anti-torture law when the government and parliament (DPR) ratify the United Nations convention against torture, the Antara news agency reported on Saturday.

"ABRI will follow the government and DPR. ABRI will support the law after the government ratifies the U.N. convention," armed forces chief General Feisal Tanjung said on Friday in the Sumatran province of Jambi.
Tanjung, asked if state authorities were ready to implement such a law, said they would follow prevailing regulations.

A member of the National Commission on Human Rights recently urged the government to make ratification of the U.N. convention a priority because of the increasing number of torture cases being reported.
The commission is currently investigating the murder of a journalist in Yogyakarta and the much publicised death last month of a robbery suspect held by police in Bogor, West Java.
"Ratification of the U.N. convention must get first priority as it embodies values which all civilised nations in the world have accepted," Antara quoted commission member Muladi as saying.
It said the leader of the ruling Golkar party faction in parliament had said the DPR was ready to ratify the anti-torture convention.
"The sooner the better, because we need it," faction chairman Moetahid Astari was quoted as saying on Thursday.
